requirements.evidence: config/services.php:40 adds 'mention_id' => env('DISCORD_MENTION_ID'); .env.example:78 adds DISCORD_MENTION_ID=. app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:73-77 reserves mb_strlen($mention)+1 from the 1800 limit, truncates only the title/message/context part and appends "\n<@id>" on its own line; limit stays 1800 when no mention. mention() (lines 65-80) accepts int or string, trims, and only matches '/\A\d{17,20}\z/' (\z plus no /u flag rejects trailing newlines and non-ASCII digits), so @everyone, @here, abc, 123 and "123\n@everyone" give ''. The send() signature is unchanged. Docs updated in docs/ops/devops.md:61,70 and docs/ops/logging.md:83.

conventions.evidence: Pest tests ship with the change (tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:124-172). Docs are kept in sync: .env.example, devops.md, logging.md, the class PHPDoc (DiscordOpsAlert.php:18-20) and CHANGELOG.md:12 under [Unreleased] > Added. It matches sibling style: `private const string` pattern constants and a private helper. No new layers.

security.evidence: The anchored snowflake regex '/\A\d{17,20}\z/' (DiscordOpsAlert.php:28) applied after trim() blocks mention injection (@everyone, newline and bracket payloads). Non-string/non-int types are rejected (line 73). Existing redaction and URL-free logging are untouched.

tests.evidence: DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:137-152 covers valid string, trimmed, integer, 17- and 20-digit IDs, and checks the mention is on its own last line. Lines 154-172 cover null, empty, blank, @everyone, @here, abc, 123, 16 and 21 digits, both injection strings from the task, a trailing @everyone, a raw mention, Arabic-Indic digits, a short int, a bool, a float and an array. Lines 174-184 check that the content is exactly 1800 characters and the mention survives truncation. No existing tests were changed.

simplicity.evidence: About 25 lines of production code: one regex constant, one small mention() helper, and a three-line change in formatContent (lines 73-77). It reuses the existing MaxContentLength and mb_substr truncation.

readability.evidence: Names are clear (mention(), SnowflakePattern, $limit). The helper has a one-line PHPDoc (line 63). The early-return style matches the class. No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: All changed files (class, config, .env.example, two ops docs, CHANGELOG, test) serve the task. There is no allowed_mentions tuning and no role mentions, both out of scope.

issues.explanation: The exact-equality check on the content already implies the two str_contains negations, so those assertions are redundant (harmless).
SnowflakePattern sits between the two redaction patterns (SecretKeyPattern and BearerLikePattern); placing it after them would keep related constants together.

review.summary: Adds an optional DISCORD_MENTION_ID / services.discord.mention_id that appends a strictly validated <@snowflake> line to every Discord ops alert. Room for the mention is reserved inside the 1800-character limit, and the env var is documented in .env.example, both ops docs and the CHANGELOG. The validation is tight, the tests are thorough (including injection and truncation cases) and the change stays minimal and in scope, so I would approve it as is.
